subject: chemistry
title: The Contact process
key_idea: (Supplement) The Contact process makes sulfur trioxide, which is used to make sulfuric acid. Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen in a reversible reaction. The typical conditions are 450 °C, 2 atmospheres (200 kPa) and a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The Contact process makes sulfur trioxide from sulfur dioxide and oxygen. This section covers where they come from and the equation.

items: (Supplement) Sulfur dioxide comes from **burning sulfur** in air.
(Supplement) It also comes from **roasting sulfide ores** in air.

blocks.label: Conversion of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide
where: The ⇌ sign shows the reaction is reversible.

diagram.alt: A flow diagram. Sulfur or a sulfide ore is burned in air to make sulfur dioxide. Sulfur dioxide and oxygen from the air react over a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst to make sulfur trioxide.

items: Sulfur dioxide comes from burning sulfur or roasting sulfide ores.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The conditions are chosen to give a good yield at a good rate. This section covers the conditions and the reasons.

items: **Temperature:** the forward reaction is exothermic, so a higher temperature lowers the yield of SO₃. A lower temperature makes the rate too slow. 450 °C is a compromise.
**Pressure:** there are three moles of gas on the left and two on the right, so a high pressure favours SO₃. A pressure lower than 2 atm gives a lower yield or a lower rate.
**Pressure:** the yield is already high at 2 atm. A much higher pressure would cost more and be more dangerous.
**Catalyst:** vanadium(V) oxide speeds up the forward and the backward reactions equally. It does not change the position of equilibrium, but the equilibrium is reached faster.
The conditions are 450 °C, 2 atm (200 kPa) and a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst.
A higher temperature lowers the yield because the forward reaction is exothermic.
A catalyst speeds up the reaction but does not change the yield.

checks.q: Name the catalyst used in the Contact process.

checks.a: Burning sulfur in air. Roasting sulfide ores in air.

checks.q: Explain why a temperature higher than 450 °C is not used.
checks.a: The forward reaction is exothermic, so a higher temperature gives a lower yield of sulfur trioxide.

worked_example.question: Sulfuric acid is manufactured in a four-stage process. In one stage, sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen to form sulfur trioxide. State three typical conditions for this reaction.
answer_points: A pressure of 2 atm or 200 kPa.
worked_example.tip: Give the number and the unit for each condition.
